rw: Correct. Diversification spreads money across stocks, bonds, cash and other asset classes, so a drop in one holding is cushioned by others, which lowers overall portfolio risk.

ww.Holding only cash forever and never buyi: Holding only cash is not diversification. Cash is one asset class, and over many years inflation steadily erodes its buying power, so growth is limited.
ww.Holding only one type of asset for the w: Holding a single type of asset is the opposite of diversification. All the money rises and falls together, leaving the investor fully exposed to one kind of risk.
ww.Holding only your employer's stock for j: Owning only your employer's stock concentrates risk in one company. If the firm struggles, both your paycheck and your investments are hurt at the same time.

rw: Correct. Owning only your employer's stock puts your paycheck and your savings at the mercy of one company, so a layoff or a stock collapse can hit both together.

ww.Less risk than a diversified fund, as th: Holding one company's stock is riskier than a diversified fund, not safer. Familiarity with the employer does not remove the chance that its share price falls sharply.
ww.No extra risk at all for the investor or: There is extra risk. Concentrating in one firm creates company-specific risk that diversification would reduce, and it ties your income and investments to the same outcome.
ww.Guaranteed high returns for the investor: Stocks never carry guaranteed returns, and a single company's shares can swing widely. High returns are possible but never promised, and losses can be large.

rw: Correct. A résumé summarizes your skills, education and work experience on one or two pages so an employer can quickly judge whether you fit the job.

ww.To apply for a bank account in your own: A bank account application uses identification and forms, not a résumé. A résumé is a career document aimed at employers, not at financial institutions.
ww.To list the prices of items you want to: A résumé does not list prices of items to buy. That would resemble a shopping or wish list, while a résumé summarizes a person's work qualifications.
ww.To record your monthly spending and your: Recording monthly spending and bank bills is the job of a budget or ledger. A résumé is a marketing document about your qualifications, not a spending record.

rw: Correct. Skills, experience and education raise a worker's productivity and scarcity, which lets them command higher pay and promotions across a career.

ww.The worker's favorite food at lunch time: A favorite lunch food has no link to earning power. Employers pay for the value of what a worker can produce, not personal food preferences.
ww.The color of the worker's car and its mo: Car color and model year are personal choices with no bearing on pay. Employers do not set wages based on what a worker drives.
ww.The number of social media posts a worke: Social media post count does not determine earnings. Employers pay for job skills and results, and heavy posting is not a qualification for higher wages.

rw: Correct. An apprenticeship combines paid on-the-job training with classroom instruction in a skilled trade such as electrician or plumber, and ends in a recognized credential.

ww.A vacation for new hires in their first: An apprenticeship is work and training, not a vacation. New hires in apprenticeships earn wages while learning a trade under experienced workers.
ww.A loan for starting a business, repaid: A loan for starting a business describes small business financing, not an apprenticeship. Apprentices are paid employees, not borrowers repaying a startup loan.
ww.A tax on skilled workers that they pay y: An apprenticeship is not a tax. Apprentices earn pay while training, and no yearly levy on skilled workers is called an apprenticeship.

rw: Correct. A self-employed person earns income from their own business or services instead of wages from an employer, and is responsible for their own taxes and benefits.

ww.Working without pay in a job that helps: Unpaid work that helps others is volunteering. Self-employment is done to earn income for yourself, not to work without pay.
ww.Working only at night in a big city fact: The time or place of work does not define self-employment. A self-employed person may work any hours, and many do not work in factories at all.
ww.Working for a large corporation that pay: Working for a corporation on salary is regular employment. A self-employed person has no employer and earns income from their own business.

rw: Correct. Being your own boss gives more control over hours, clients and business decisions, though it also brings less stable income and more responsibility.

ww.Employer-paid benefits such as health in: Self-employed people usually pay for their own health insurance. Employer-paid benefits are a feature of regular jobs, not self-employment.
ww.No need to pay taxes on the income that: Self-employed workers still owe income tax and also pay both halves of Social Security and Medicare through self-employment tax, so taxes are not avoided.
ww.Guaranteed steady income, as pay is the: Self-employed income often rises and falls with customers and seasons. A guaranteed, unchanging paycheck is more typical of a salaried job.

rw: Correct. Unemployment insurance, funded by employer payroll taxes, gives temporary income to eligible workers laid off or let go through no fault of their own while they look for work.

ww.A bonus for finding a job that the gover: Unemployment insurance is not a bonus for finding work. It pays eligible workers a temporary benefit while they are out of a job and searching.
ww.A refund of payroll taxes paid back to a: It is not a refund of payroll taxes at retirement. Retirement income comes from Social Security, while unemployment insurance pays weekly benefits after a job loss.
ww.A loan for job seekers from the state th: It is not a loan and nothing is repaid with interest. Benefits are funded by employer payroll taxes and given to eligible workers who were laid off.

rw: Correct. A merit raise rewards an employee's strong performance or achievements with higher pay, unlike an across-the-board raise given to everyone or a cost-of-living adjustment.

ww.An increase given automatically to every: An increase given automatically to everyone is a general or across-the-board raise, not a merit raise, which depends on individual performance.
ww.A fee paid to the employer for the raise: A raise is paid by the employer to the worker. The employee does not pay the employer a fee for receiving a merit raise.
ww.A cut in pay given for poor results over: A cut in pay for poor results is a pay reduction or penalty. A merit raise is an increase tied to good performance.

rw: Correct. A 3% raise matches 3% price growth, so your income keeps pace with costs and your real buying power stays about the same.

ww.It falls sharply by a lot: With a 3% raise against 3% inflation, purchasing power does not fall sharply. The extra pay offsets the higher prices almost exactly.
ww.It rises sharply every year: A raise equal to inflation does not boost buying power. Prices rose by the same 3%, so extra income buys no more than before.
ww.It disappears from your pay: Buying power does not vanish. Your pay still buys about the same goods as before because the raise matches the 3% price increase.

rw: Correct. An unplanned expense is an unexpected cost, such as a car repair or medical bill, which an emergency fund is designed to cover.

ww.A cost that is zero in every single mont: A cost that is zero every month would not be an expense at all. An unplanned expense is a real cost, just one you did not budget for.
ww.A cost you pay every month on the first: A cost paid on the first of each month is a recurring fixed expense such as rent, which is planned in advance, not unplanned.
ww.A cost in your budget, such as the rent: Rent paid each month is a planned fixed expense already in your budget. Unplanned expenses are the ones you did not see coming.

rw: Correct. An emergency fund is cash saved for surprises like a $120 repair, letting you pay immediately without borrowing or paying interest.

ww.Ignoring the repair: Ignoring a broken screen does not solve the problem and may leave you without a working phone. It is not a way to pay for the repair.
ww.A payday loan: A payday loan carries very high fees and interest, so borrowing $120 this way creates more debt. It is the opposite of paying without debt.
ww.A new credit card: A new credit card means borrowing, so the $120 becomes debt with interest if not repaid in full. It does not avoid debt.

rw: Correct. Loyalty programs reward purchases with points or discounts, which can tempt shoppers to buy more than planned just to earn rewards.

ww.It always raises prices in the shop for: Loyalty programs do not raise prices for everyone. They offer members discounts or points, and the drawback is overspending, not higher shelf prices.
ww.It bans returns of any kind for all the: Joining a loyalty program does not ban returns. Return policies are set separately by the store and are not removed by membership.
ww.It removes all discounts, so members pay: Loyalty programs usually add member discounts, not remove them. Members do not have to pay full price, so this is not their drawback.

rw: Correct. Shopping around means comparing prices, quality and terms at several sellers so you can pick the best value for your money.

ww.Buy the most expensive item that you can: Buying the most expensive item is the opposite of shopping around. Shopping around aims to find the best value, often at a lower price.
ww.Walk around the shop without buying anyt: Walking through a shop without buying is browsing. Shopping around means actively comparing prices and quality among sellers before deciding.
ww.Buy from the first seller you meet to sa: Buying from the first seller skips comparison entirely. Saving time may cost more money because you never learn whether better prices exist.

rw: Correct. If a return is possible, free returns protect you. A failed $72 purchase is a total loss, while the $80 pair can be refunded.

ww.They are identical in every way: The two offers are not identical. The $80 headphones include free returns while the $72 pair allow none, so the protection differs even if the product matches.
ww.Neither store is the better deal: One store is better when you may need to return the item. Free returns have real value, so the two are not equal for this buyer.
ww.The $72 store, as its price is low: The lower price saves $8 but gives up return protection. If the headphones are defective or unwanted, the $72 would be wasted.

rw: Correct. A service charge is a fee a bank charges, such as a monthly maintenance fee, for running and servicing the account.

ww.A tax on interest earned in the account: A tax on interest is an income tax matter, not a service charge. A service charge is a fee the bank itself charges for account services.
ww.A reward for opening an account, like a: A reward for opening an account is a sign-up bonus. A service charge costs the customer money rather than giving a gift.
ww.A loan payment made each month to the ba: A monthly loan payment goes toward borrowed money. A service charge is a fee for account services, not a loan repayment.

rw: Correct. A purchase limit caps how much a debit card can spend in a period, which reduces losses if the card is lost or stolen.

ww.Raising your credit score by showing how: Debit cards do not build credit scores because they use your own money rather than borrowed credit. A spending cap has nothing to do with scores.
ww.Earning interest on the money in your ca: Purchase limits do not earn interest. Interest on an account comes from the bank paying you on balances, not from a spending cap.
ww.Paying taxes on the money you spend with: A purchase limit does not pay taxes. Sales tax is added at checkout, and the limit only restricts how much you can spend.

rw: Correct. A goal-based plan sets target amounts and dates, such as $2,400 in 8 months, so you know how much to save each period.

ww.Saving random amounts with no aim in min: Saving random amounts with no aim lacks goals. A goal-based plan names specific targets, amounts and deadlines.
ww.Spending all income first, then saving w: Spending first and saving leftovers is the opposite of a planned approach. Goal-based saving sets money aside first for each goal.
ww.Never saving any money for any goal at a: Never saving for any goal is not a plan at all. It leaves nothing for emergencies or purchases, the opposite of goal-based saving.

rw: Correct. Divide the goal by the months: $2,400 / 8 = $300 per month, so saving $300 monthly reaches the laptop in 8 months.

ww.$19,200: $19,200 comes from multiplying $2,400 by 8 instead of dividing. The monthly amount must be far smaller than the total goal.
ww.$3,000: $3,000 does not match the goal. Saving $3,000 a month for 8 months would total $24,000, ten times the $2,400 needed.
ww.$30: $30 a month for 8 months saves only $240, one tenth of the $2,400 target. The decimal is misplaced.

rw: Correct. Series I savings bonds pay a rate that combines a fixed rate with an inflation rate adjusted twice a year, protecting buying power against rising prices.

ww.Bank failure: Bank failure is covered by FDIC insurance, not by I bonds. I bonds are backed by the US government but are designed for inflation protection.
ww.High taxes: I bonds do not shield you from taxes in general. Interest is exempt from state and local tax, but their design purpose is inflation protection.
ww.Stock losses: I bonds are not tied to stock markets, so they do not guard against stock losses. Their rate adjusts with inflation instead.

rw: Correct. A credit union is a not-for-profit cooperative owned by its members, and its savings accounts typically offer competitive rates and low fees.

ww.An account that is not insured by anyone: Credit union accounts are federally insured, up to $250,000 per depositor, by the NCUA. They are not uninsured.
ww.A savings account held at a for-profit s: A for-profit stock exchange firm is not a credit union. Credit unions are not-for-profit and owned by their members, not by outside shareholders.
ww.A loan from a union that helps its worke: A savings account is a deposit product, not a loan. A credit union is a financial cooperative, not an arm of a labor union.

rw: Correct. The NCUA, through the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund, insures member deposits at federal credit unions up to $250,000 per depositor.

ww.The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) offic: The IRS collects federal taxes and does not insure bank or credit union deposits. Deposit insurance is handled by other agencies.
ww.The Social Security Administration (SSA): The SSA runs Social Security retirement and disability benefits. It does not insure deposits at credit unions.
ww.The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) offic: The FTC protects consumers from unfair business practices and enforces competition law. It does not insure deposits at credit unions.

rw: Correct. Liquid assets, such as cash or a savings account, can be converted to cash quickly with little or no loss of value.

ww.It is stored as water in a tank: Liquid does not mean stored as water. In finance, liquidity describes how easily an asset converts into cash, not its physical form.
ww.It never changes in value over time: Liquidity does not mean a stable value. A liquid asset may still change in price; the term only concerns how quickly it becomes cash.
ww.It cannot be spent at all by anyone: Liquid money can be spent easily. An asset that cannot be spent is illiquid, the opposite of liquid.

rw: Correct. Savings accounts allow you to withdraw cash almost any time with little or no penalty, making them highly liquid.

ww.A plot of city land: Land takes time to sell and its price can vary, so it is illiquid. It cannot be turned into cash quickly.
ww.A five-year CD: A five-year CD locks money until maturity, and early withdrawal usually triggers a penalty, so it is less liquid than a savings account.
ww.A house in a city: A house can take months to sell and has transaction costs, so it is one of the least liquid assets people own.

rw: Correct. Credit utilization is the share of available credit you use. High utilization suggests heavy borrowing and tends to lower your credit score.

ww.It deletes old debt from the lender: Utilization does not delete debt. It measures how much of your credit limit you are using and never erases balances owed.
ww.High utilization raises your score: High utilization hurts rather than helps. Lenders see heavy use of available credit as a sign of risk, so scores generally drop.
ww.It has no effect on your credit score: Credit utilization has a strong effect on credit scores. It is one of the main factors, typically about thirty percent of a FICO score.

rw: Correct. Payment history and utilization are the biggest score factors, so on-time payments and low balances steadily build a stronger credit score.

ww.Maxing out your credit cards each month: Maxing out cards drives credit utilization high, which lowers your score. Lenders see it as risky borrowing.
ww.Missing payments on your bills now and t: Missed payments are reported to credit bureaus and damage scores. Payment history is the largest factor in most scoring models.
ww.Closing all old accounts to cut your his: Closing all old accounts shortens credit history and cuts available credit, which usually raises utilization and lowers your score.

rw: Correct. A deferred payment plan lets you buy now and pay later, often with interest charged if the balance is not paid in full by the due date.

ww.A gift of free goods that the seller han: A gift of free goods is a giveaway. A deferred payment plan is a credit arrangement where you buy now and pay later.
ww.A tax refund paid by the state to a pers: A tax refund is money returned by the government. A deferred payment plan is a seller's offer, not a government payment.
ww.An interest-free loan that you never hav: A deferred payment plan is not a gift loan. You must pay the seller what you owe, and many plans charge interest if unpaid on time.

rw: Correct. With deferred interest, if any balance remains after month 12, interest is charged back to the purchase date, which can mean a large sudden cost.

ww.The offer improves your credit score aut: Such an offer does not automatically improve your credit score. Credit history depends on how you manage the account, not on the promotion.
ww.The seller pays your interest for the wh: The seller does not pay your interest. With deferred interest, the interest builds in the background and is charged to you if you miss the deadline.
ww.No risk at all if you miss the final pay: Missing the final date carries real risk. The retroactive interest can be added to your balance, so the offer is risky if unpaid in time.

rw: Correct. At the same rate, a shorter 3-year term means the balance falls faster and interest accrues for fewer months, so total interest is lower.

ww.They cost the same: The two loans do not cost the same. With the same rate, the longer term accrues interest for more months and costs more overall.
ww.The 5-year loan: The 5-year loan has smaller payments but higher total interest, because the principal is outstanding longer. Its total cost is greater, not lower.
ww.Neither loan costs: Both loans charge interest at a stated rate, so each costs something. The 3-year loan simply costs less overall than the 5-year loan.

rw: Correct. A copayment is a fixed fee, such as $25, that you pay at the time of a covered service while the insurer pays the rest.

ww.A fine for missing an appointment with a: A fine for a missed appointment is a no-show or cancellation fee, which is separate from the copay charged for covered services.
ww.The yearly total you pay for insurance,: The yearly total you pay for insurance, billed in monthly parts, is the premium. A copayment is paid per service when care is received.
ww.The insurer's profit on each policy that: The insurer's profit on policies is not the copayment. A copay is the customer's fixed share of the cost of a covered service.

rw: Correct. Each visit costs a $25 copay, so 4 visits cost 4 x $25 = $100.

ww.$29: $29 adds 4 to $25, which is not how copays work. Each visit costs $25, so you multiply the copay by the number of visits.
ww.$25: $25 is the copay for only one visit. With 4 visits you owe this amount four times.
ww.$6.25: $6.25 comes from dividing $25 by 4. The copay applies to each visit, so you multiply rather than divide.

rw: Correct. With 20% coinsurance you pay 20% of the bill: 0.20 x $2,000 = $400, and the insurer covers the other $1,600.

ww.$1,600: $1,600 is the insurer's share, which is 80% of $2,000. Coinsurance means you pay the 20% that remains.
ww.$40: $40 would be 2% of $2,000, a decimal slip. Twenty percent of $2,000 is much larger.
ww.$2,000: Paying the full $2,000 ignores insurance. After the deductible, coinsurance means the insurer covers its percentage, so you owe only your share.

rw: Correct. Long-term care insurance pays for extended services such as nursing homes, assisted living or home health aides, which regular health insurance often does not cover.

ww.Coverage for home theft and burglary los: Theft and burglary losses are covered by homeowners or renters insurance. Long-term care insurance covers personal care needs, not property.
ww.Coverage for a short hospital stay only,: Short hospital stays fall under health insurance. Long-term care insurance covers extended help with daily living, often over months or years.
ww.Coverage for car repairs after a bad acc: Car repairs after an accident belong to auto insurance. Long-term care insurance has nothing to do with vehicles.

rw: Correct. Extended care can cost tens of thousands per year, and long-term care insurance helps protect retirement savings from being drained by those bills.

ww.To avoid ever needing care of any kind i: Insurance cannot prevent the need for care. It only helps pay for care if the need arises in later life.
ww.To pay for groceries and other everyday: Everyday groceries are regular living costs not paid by insurance. Long-term care policies cover extended care services only.
ww.To lower their taxes to zero, since prem: Premiums are not a way to cut taxes to zero. Some may be partly deductible, but no deduction brings a tax bill to zero.

rw: Correct. In a no-fault state, each driver's own insurer pays for their injuries up to a set limit regardless of who caused the crash, which speeds up claims.

ww.A state where only the at-fault driver i: That describes a traditional at-fault system, where the responsible driver's insurer pays. In no-fault states each insurer pays its own policyholder.
ww.A state where no one needs insurance for: Almost every state requires some auto insurance, including no-fault states, so no state lets all drivers go without coverage.
ww.A state where insurers never pay any cla: No-fault insurers do pay claims. The term means fault does not decide whose insurer pays for injuries, not that claims are denied.

rw: Correct. If a car is totaled or stolen, regular insurance pays only its market value, and gap insurance covers the remaining loan balance.

ww.Coverage for gaps in your teeth that nee: Gap insurance has nothing to do with teeth or dental care. It is an auto coverage that handles a loan shortfall after a total loss.
ww.Coverage for routine repairs and servici: Routine repairs and servicing are maintenance costs, sometimes covered by a service contract, not by gap insurance.
ww.Coverage for gaps in your schedule when: Gap insurance is not about schedule gaps. It covers the money difference between what the car is worth and the loan balance.

rw: Correct. The insurer pays the $14,000 value, leaving $18,000 - $14,000 = $4,000 owed on the loan, which gap insurance covers.

ww.Nothing at all is owed: Something is owed. The lender still expects the $18,000 balance, and the insurer pays only the car's $14,000 value.
ww.The full $18,000 loan: Gap insurance does not pay the full loan. The regular policy covers the car's value of $14,000, and gap covers only the shortfall.
ww.A new set of car tires: New tires are a maintenance item and not covered by gap insurance, which concerns only the loan balance beyond the car's value.

rw: Correct. Volatility describes how widely and quickly a price swings, and high volatility means larger gains or losses over short periods.

ww.How long the company has existed since i: How long a company has existed is its age or track record, not the volatility of its stock price.
ww.How much dividend it pays out each year: Dividends paid to owners describe income, not volatility. A stock can pay large dividends and still have a stable price.
ww.How many shares exist in the whole compa: The number of shares is its shares outstanding. Volatility measures price movement, not share count.

rw: Correct. A single small-company stock depends on one business, with less stability and thinner trading, so its price can swing widely.

ww.A short-term Treasury bill: A Treasury bill is backed by the US government and has a short term, so its price barely moves. It is among the least volatile.
ww.A federally insured account: Federally insured accounts keep their value because of deposit insurance. Their balances do not swing, so they are not volatile.
ww.A broad bond index fund today: A broad bond index fund holds many bonds and tends to move gently, so it is far less volatile than one small stock.

rw: Correct. Buy and hold means purchasing investments and keeping them through market ups and downs, aiming for long-term growth with lower trading costs.

ww.Buying only on margin with money borrowe: Buying on margin means borrowing from a broker, which adds risk. Buy and hold is about keeping investments, not borrowing to buy them.
ww.Buying and selling every day to gain fro: Buying and selling daily is day trading. Buy and hold is the opposite approach of staying invested for years.
ww.Selling after one week of holding your i: Selling after one week is short-term trading. Buy and hold needs a long horizon, often years or decades.

rw: Correct. A dividend reinvestment plan automatically uses cash dividends to buy more shares, often with no commission, which lets holdings compound over time.

ww.A plan that sells shares automatically e: A DRIP does not sell shares on a schedule. It does the opposite by using dividends to purchase more shares.
ww.A plan that sends all dividends from the: A DRIP keeps the dividends invested in the same company rather than sending them to charity. Giving to charity is a separate choice.
ww.A plan that cancels dividends paid to al: A DRIP does not cancel dividends. The company still pays them, and the plan simply turns them into additional shares.

rw: Correct. Dividends are paid per share, so 50 shares x $1 per share = $50 received.

ww.$0.02: $0.02 is a tiny number from a decimal mistake. The dividend is $1 per share across 50 shares, so the total is much higher.
ww.$5,000: $5,000 comes from multiplying by 5,000 instead of 50. The correct total is far smaller than this.
ww.$1: $1 is the dividend for only one share. You own 50 shares, so you receive that amount fifty times.

rw: Correct. Yield is the return an investor earns on a bond, often shown as a percent of its price, such as current yield or yield to maturity.

ww.The date the bond ends and the principal: The date the principal is due back is the maturity date, not the yield. Yield is a rate of return.
ww.The fee paid to a broker when the bond i: The fee paid to a broker is a commission or markup. It is a cost of trading rather than the bond's return.
ww.The amount borrowed by the issuer when t: The amount borrowed by the issuer is the bond's principal or face value, not the yield an investor earns.

rw: Correct. A savings bond is a loan to the government that pays interest, while a stock is partial ownership of a company and may pay dividends.

ww.Both are ownership in a company, and bot: Savings bonds are loans to the government, not ownership in a company, and they pay interest rather than dividends.
ww.Both are loans to the government, and bo: Stocks are not loans to the government, and they pay no fixed interest. Only the bond part of this statement is right.
ww.They are the same thing, as both are sha: They are different. A stock is an ownership share in a company, while a savings bond is a debt the government owes you.

rw: Correct. A short-term CD or Treasury security returns principal and a known interest rate within a short period, so there is little risk of loss by the date needed.

ww.Cryptocurrency and coins: Cryptocurrency prices can swing sharply in days, so it is a poor choice for money needed in two years.
ww.A stock pick on margin funds: Buying a stock on margin uses borrowed money and magnifies losses, which is unsuitable for a short two-year goal.
ww.A single risky stock pick: One risky stock can fall sharply with no time to recover. With a two-year horizon it is too uncertain to be considered safe.

rw: Correct. The spread is the gap between the highest price a buyer will pay (bid) and the lowest a seller will accept (ask), and it is a hidden trading cost.

ww.The tax on trades of stocks, bonds and f: A tax on trades is a transaction or capital gains tax, not a spread, which is a price difference inside the market.
ww.The size of a company in the stock marke: A company's size in the market is its market capitalization. The spread concerns the bid and ask quotes of a security.
ww.The number of shares traded on the excha: The number of shares traded is trading volume. The spread is measured in price, not in shares.

rw: Correct. Before a large credit purchase, make sure the payments fit your budget, including interest, so the debt does not strain your finances.

ww.Choose the card with the largest limit y: The largest limit does not make a purchase affordable. A high limit can tempt you to borrow more than you can repay.
ww.Ignore the interest rate and the fees yo: Ignoring interest and fees hides the true cost of credit. Interest can add a lot to the price, so it must be weighed.
ww.Buy it first and plan the payments later: Buying first and planning payments later risks missed payments and debt. Budgeting should come before taking on credit.

rw: Correct. Income, expenses and goals change over time, so reviewing your savings plan once or twice a year keeps it realistic and on track.

ww.Plans never need any changes at all, eve: Plans do need changes. A raise, a new expense or a different goal can all make an older plan out of date.
ww.Banks require a new plan from every cust: Banks do not require customers to make new savings plans. Reviewing your plan is a personal habit, not a bank rule.
ww.Reviews remove the need to save any mone: Reviewing a plan does not replace saving. It checks that your saving amounts still match your goals so you keep saving.

rw: Correct. Gross pay is hourly rate times hours worked: $18 x 35 = $630 before taxes and deductions.

ww.$18: $18 is her pay for one hour only. She worked 35 hours, so you must multiply the hourly rate by hours worked.
ww.$6,300: $6,300 comes from a decimal error multiplying by 350. Gross pay is $18 x 35, far less than this.
ww.$53: $53 adds the rate and hours: 18 + 35. Pay is found by multiplying, not adding.

rw: Correct. Wages are paid by the hour, so pay varies with hours worked, while a salary is a fixed amount for each pay period regardless of hours.

ww.A wage is paid yearly and a salary is pa: This reverses the definitions. A wage is paid hourly and a salary is paid as a fixed yearly amount.
ww.A salary is only for part-time work, whi: Salary and wage are not tied to part-time or full-time work. Either type of pay can apply to both kinds of jobs.
ww.A wage is always higher than a salary, f: Neither is always higher. Which pays more depends on the job, the hours worked and the rate agreed with the employer.

rw: Correct. Net pay equals gross pay minus deductions: $1,200 - $240 = $960, the amount she takes home.

ww.$240: $240 is only the deductions. Net pay is what remains after subtracting those deductions from gross pay.
ww.$1,200: $1,200 is the gross pay before deductions. Net pay is lower after the $240 is taken out.
ww.$1,440: $1,440 adds the deductions to gross pay: $1,200 + $240. Deductions are subtracted, not added.

rw: Correct. FICA stands for Federal Insurance Contributions Act and covers the Social Security and Medicare taxes withheld from your paycheck.

ww.Net pay: Net pay is the amount left after withholdings, so it is not the line showing money withheld for Social Security and Medicare.
ww.Gross: Gross is total pay before anything is withheld, so it cannot show Social Security and Medicare contributions.
ww.Hours: Hours shows time worked, not money withheld. It does not itemize any tax deductions on the pay stub.

rw: Correct. Overtime is extra pay, usually 1.5 times the regular rate, for hours worked beyond a standard limit such as 40 hours a week.

ww.A bonus for arriving early at work each: A bonus for arriving early is a punctuality incentive. Overtime relates to extra hours worked, not to arrival time.
ww.Pay for vacation days that you have take: Pay for vacation days taken off is paid time off. Overtime is for additional hours actually worked.
ww.A tax refund paid at the end of each yea: A year-end tax refund is money returned by the government. Overtime is earned pay from extra hours.

rw: Correct. 40 hours x $20 = $800, plus 4 overtime hours x $30 ($20 x 1.5) = $120, so the total is $920.

ww.$880: $880 pays all 44 hours at the regular $20 rate. Overtime hours should earn time and a half, so pay is higher.
ww.$960: $960 pays all 48 hours worked at regular pay or miscounts the overtime. Only 4 hours earn the $30 rate.
ww.$800: $800 counts only the first 40 hours and leaves out the 4 overtime hours, which add 4 x $30 = $120.

rw: Correct. Health insurance is a common employer benefit, with the employer often paying part of the cost on top of the worker's wages.

ww.A parking ticket: A parking ticket is a fine, a cost to the driver, not a benefit offered by an employer.
ww.A delivery charge: A delivery charge is a fee for shipping goods and is not a benefit employers offer.
ww.A late fee charge: A late fee is a penalty for paying after the due date and is a cost, not a benefit.

rw: Correct. The percent change is the raise divided by the old wage: $2 / $16 = 0.125, or 12.5%.

ww.16.0%: 16.0% comes from mixing up the numbers. Divide the $2 raise by the original $16 wage, which gives 12.5%.
ww.2%: 2% takes the dollar amount as a percent. The raise is $2, which is a larger share of a $16 wage.
ww.50%: 50% is far too large. A $2 raise on a $16 wage is only one eighth of the old wage.

rw: Correct. More education and skills make workers more productive and qualified for higher-paying jobs, which raises lifetime earnings on average.

ww.Education prevents job changes, since de: Education does not prevent job changes. It usually opens more job options, so degree holders often have more choices.
ww.Education lowers all pay, since schoolin: Education does not lower pay. Though schooling costs time and money, higher education generally leads to higher lifetime earnings.
ww.Employers ignore skills and look only at: Employers value skills and qualifications. Hair color and height are not legitimate pay factors and may not be used to discriminate.

rw: Correct. Self-employment income is the profit a person earns from their own business or freelance work, rather than wages from an employer.

ww.A lottery prize won by chance on a ticke: A lottery prize comes from chance, not from working. Self-employment income is earned by operating a business.
ww.A tax refund paid by the state to a work: A tax refund is money returned by the government, not income earned from running a business.
ww.Money from a parent's allowance paid to: An allowance from a parent is a gift of money. Self-employment income is earned from your own work.

rw: Correct. No tax is withheld from freelance pay, so without setting money aside the freelancer may face a large bill, plus possible penalties, at filing time.

ww.A refund of tax, as freelancers get brea: Freelancers do not get tax refunds for skipping payments. They owe self-employment and income taxes, so setting nothing aside is risky.
ww.No tax obligation at all this year or ne: Freelancers have a tax obligation. Self-employment income is taxed, and estimated payments are usually due quarterly.
ww.Lower income next year than in this year: Not saving for taxes does not by itself change next year's income. The issue is an unexpected tax bill, not lower earnings.

rw: Correct. Gig work is short-term or task-based work, such as ride-share driving or delivery, often found through an app, with workers paid per task.

ww.A government benefit paid out to people: A government benefit for people out of work is unemployment insurance. A gig job is work you perform for pay.
ww.A volunteer role with no pay at a charit: A volunteer role has no pay, whereas a gig job pays for each task completed.
ww.A permanent salaried role with a fixed w: A permanent salaried role with benefits is a standard full-time job, the opposite of a temporary gig.

rw: Correct. A résumé gap is a period without paid work. Be honest and briefly explain what you did, such as study, caregiving or volunteering.

ww.A mistake to hide from every employer th: A résumé gap should not be hidden. Employers notice gaps, and being honest about them builds trust.
ww.A reason never to apply, as employers hi: Employers do hire people with résumé gaps. Gaps from school, family or illness are common, and a clear explanation helps.
ww.A required legal form that every worker: A résumé gap is not a legal form. It is simply a time period without listed employment.

rw: Correct. Both pay $40,000, but Job B adds $5,000 of insurance, so total compensation is $45,000 versus $40,000.

ww.They are always exactly identical: The two are not identical. Job B includes $5,000 in benefits that Job A lacks, so total compensation differs.
ww.Job A, because it has fewer parts: Fewer parts do not make compensation higher. Job A offers salary only, so its total of $40,000 is lower than Job B's $45,000.
ww.Neither one has any compensation: Both jobs pay a salary, so each has compensation. Job B simply has more once benefits are included.

rw: Correct. A probation period is an initial time, often 30 to 90 days, when the employer reviews performance before confirming the job permanently.

ww.A permanent guarantee of keeping the job: A probation period gives no guarantee of keeping the job. The employer is evaluating whether the worker fits the position.
ww.A tax break for new workers in the first: Probation is not a tax break. It is an employment term and has no connection to taxes.
ww.A long paid vacation for new workers eac: Probation is not a vacation. New workers are usually working and often get limited or no time off in that period.

rw: Correct. Take-home pay, also called net pay, is what remains after taxes and deductions are subtracted from gross pay.

ww.Pay before taxes and any deductions: Pay before taxes and deductions is gross pay. Take-home pay is lower than that amount.
ww.The hours worked in each pay period: Hours worked in a pay period measure time, not money. Take-home pay is a dollar amount.
ww.A company's profit for the whole year ah: A company's yearly profit is a business measure. Take-home pay refers to an individual worker's paycheck.

rw: Correct. Volunteering and other activities build skills and references, and a clear résumé presents them, which raises hiring chances even without paid experience.

ww.Skip applications and just wait for a jo: Skipping applications and waiting means employers never see her. Jobs go to people who actively apply.
ww.Refuse every interview that you are ever: Refusing every interview removes her chance to get hired. Interviews are how employers choose new workers.
ww.Apply with no contact details at all on: A résumé without contact details prevents employers from reaching her, so it greatly reduces her chances.

rw: Correct. 25% of $60 is $15, so the sale price is $60 - $15 = $45.

ww.$15: $15 is the amount of the discount (25% of $60), not the price. The sale price is the original price minus the discount.
ww.$35: $35 subtracts 25 dollars instead of 25 percent. The discount is a percentage of $60.
ww.$75: $75 adds the discount to the price. A sale lowers the price, so it must go down from $60.

rw: Correct. An impulse purchase is an unplanned, spur-of-the-moment buy, such as grabbing candy at the checkout, usually triggered by display or emotion.

ww.Paying rent on the first day of every mo: Rent is a planned monthly obligation. Impulse purchases are unplanned buys made on the spur of the moment.
ww.Buying groceries from a planned weekly l: Groceries bought from a planned weekly list are deliberate, planned purchases, not impulse buys.
ww.Saving for a bike over months from each: Saving over months for a bike is planned, goal-based spending, the opposite of an impulse purchase.

rw: Correct. The monthly plan costs 24 x $25 = $600, which is $120 more than paying $480 up front.

ww.$480: $480 is the up-front price only. The monthly plan costs more in total because 24 payments of $25 add up to more.
ww.$120: $120 is the difference between the plan and the cash price, not the plan's total cost.
ww.$49: $49 adds 24 and 25. Total cost comes from multiplying the monthly payment by the number of months.

rw: Correct. Unit price is the cost per single unit, such as per ounce or per item, which lets you compare different package sizes fairly.

ww.The tax on a purchase at the store till: Tax on a purchase is sales tax. Unit price is about the cost per unit of measure.
ww.The price after a coupon is applied at c: The price after a coupon is the final or discounted price, not the unit price.
ww.The total cost of everything in a shoppi: The total cost of a shopping cart is the cart total. Unit price is a per-unit value.

rw: Correct. Receipts are proof of purchase for returns, warranty claims and tracking spending in your budget.

ww.They raise the item's price, as stores c: Stores do not charge for receipts. Receipts record what you paid and do not raise an item's price.
ww.They replace warranties and stores' retu: Receipts do not replace warranties or return policies. They support them by proving when and where you bought the item.
ww.They are never needed for returns or for: Receipts are often required for returns and warranty claims, since they prove the purchase.

rw: Correct. $9.00 / 20 = $0.45 per juice, which is lower than $6.00 / 12 = $0.50, so the 20-pack is the better value.

ww.The 12-pack at $0.50 each: The 12-pack costs $6.00 / 12 = $0.50 each, which is higher than the 20-pack's unit price.
ww.The 12-pack at $0.40 each: $0.40 is a miscalculation. $6.00 divided by 12 is $0.50 per juice.
ww.They cost the same per juice: The two sizes do not cost the same per juice. $0.50 versus $0.45 shows the 20-pack is cheaper.

rw: Correct. A budget category groups related expenses, such as food, housing or transportation, so you can plan and track spending in each area.

ww.A bank fee charged for using a machine a: A fee for using another bank's machine is an ATM fee, not a budget category.
ww.A type of loan from a bank that is repai: A loan repaid in installments is an installment loan. A budget category is a planning group.
ww.A tax return line that lists the income: An income line on a tax return is not a budget category, which is used for planning spending.

rw: Correct. $40 - $5 = $35 after the coupon, and tax is 8% x $35 = $2.80, so the total is $35 + $2.80 = $37.80.

ww.$43.20: $43.20 applies the 8% tax to the full $40 price without the coupon. Tax here is applied after the coupon.
ww.$45.00: $45.00 adds the coupon amount to the price instead of subtracting it, which is not how a coupon works.
ww.$35.00: $35.00 is the price after the coupon but before tax. The 8% sales tax must still be added.

rw: Correct. Researching prices, reading reviews and checking your budget helps you decide whether the purchase is wise and affordable.

ww.Ignore your budget and all of the prices: Ignoring prices and your budget leads to overspending. A good first step involves gathering information.
ww.Ask a stranger to pay so the cost is sha: Asking a stranger to pay is unrealistic and not a financial plan. You are responsible for your own purchases.
ww.Buy immediately without a plan or a budg: Buying immediately without a plan is an impulse purchase, which can cause regret and debt.

rw: Correct. Daily cost times days gives $15 x 20 = $300 spent on lunch in the month.

ww.$35: $35 adds 15 and 20. Her spending is the daily cost times the number of days, so multiply.
ww.$150: $150 is only 10 days of lunches. She buys lunch on 20 workdays, so the total must be larger.
ww.$600: $600 uses 40 days or a doubling error. $15 x 20 workdays is lower.

rw: Correct. Paying with cash limits spending to what you actually have, which helps prevent overspending and debt.

ww.It is safe from loss or theft anywhere: Cash can be lost or stolen and has no fraud protection, so it is not safe from loss anywhere.
ww.It earns rewards like points on purchase: Cash does not earn reward points. Rewards come from credit cards or loyalty programs.
ww.It builds a credit history over time for: Paying cash does not build credit history. Credit history comes from borrowing and repaying credit.

rw: Correct. $9.99 x 12 months = $119.88, which is about $120 wasted on a service she did not use.

ww.$10 a year: $10 is roughly one month of the subscription, not the full year. It is paid every month.
ww.$1,200 total: $1,200 is ten times too high, a decimal slip. Twelve payments of about $10 total about $120.
ww.$12 a year: $12 is a miscalculation of the year's cost. Twelve monthly payments of $9.99 total about $120.

rw: Correct. Buyer's remorse is the regret or doubt a person feels after making a purchase, often after an impulse buy.

ww.A discount only for new buyers: A discount for new buyers is a promotion. Buyer's remorse is a feeling, not a price offer.
ww.A product defect found by buyers: A defect is a product fault. Buyer's remorse is an emotional response, not a fault in the item.
ww.A credit score after a purchase: A credit score is a number that rates borrowing history. Buyer's remorse is a feeling after buying.

rw: Correct. Paying cash for a reliable used car avoids interest and depreciation of a new car, and saved money can go to savings.

ww.Skipping insurance to save money in the: Skipping insurance leaves you exposed to large costs from accidents or illness, which can damage long-term finances.
ww.Taking a loan for every purchase that yo: Borrowing for every purchase builds debt and interest costs, which hurt long-term financial health.
ww.Buying the priciest car on credit, so th: Buying the priciest car on credit adds large, long-lasting payments and interest, which strains finances for years.

rw: Correct. Store credit is value issued when you return an item, which can be used only at that store, rather than a cash refund.

ww.A paycheck that an employer issues to a: A paycheck from an employer is wages for work, not a store credit.
ww.A tax refund that the government sends a: A tax refund is money returned by the government and is not issued by a store.
ww.A bank loan that a customer repays in mo: A bank loan repaid monthly is an installment loan. Store credit is a balance given for a return.

rw: Correct. A shopping list keeps you focused on planned items, which helps you avoid unplanned purchases and stay within your budget.

ww.It increases prices in the shop a lot: A shopping list does not increase prices. It helps you buy only what you planned.
ww.It makes shopping take much longer: A list usually makes shopping faster and more focused because you know what to buy.
ww.It removes the need for any budget: A shopping list does not replace a budget. It supports it by guiding spending decisions.

rw: Correct. Peer pressure affects spending when people buy things just because friends have them, rather than because they need or can afford them.

ww.Paying less because of a big sale at the: Paying less because of a big sale reflects a price promotion, not social influence from friends.
ww.Saving because your friends ask you to s: Saving because friends ask you to save is positive social influence on saving, not an effect on spending.
ww.Having more income than most of your fri: Having more income than friends describes your income level, which is not a pressure effect.

rw: Correct. She keeps $120 - $90 = $30, and $30 / $120 = 0.25, so she keeps 25% of her income.

ww.30%: 30% mistakes the $30 she keeps for a percent. The share kept is $30 divided by the $120 income, which is 25%, not 30%.
ww.90%: 90% confuses $90 spent with the percent kept. She keeps only the money left after spending.
ww.75%: 75% is the share she spends, since $90 / $120 = 75%. The share she keeps is the rest.

rw: Correct. Negotiating means discussing with a seller to reach a lower or fair price, often by comparing prices and asking politely.

ww.Argue loudly with the seller until they: Arguing loudly is not negotiation. Negotiation is a respectful discussion aimed at an agreement both sides accept.
ww.Pay the sticker price only, without disc: Paying the sticker price without discussion skips negotiation entirely.
ww.Refuse to buy anything from the seller a: Refusing to buy anything from the seller is not negotiation. It ends discussion rather than seeking an agreement.

rw: Correct. A hidden fee is a charge not clearly disclosed at the start, such as a service or processing fee, which raises the final price.

ww.A refund of the money that you spent: A refund returns money you spent. A hidden fee is an added charge you did not know about.
ww.A discount on a coupon given by a store: A discount on a coupon lowers the price. A hidden fee raises your cost.
ww.A tax shown on the receipt at the bottom: A tax listed on the receipt is a disclosed sales tax, not a hidden fee.

rw: Correct. Waiting 24 hours gives time to judge whether you truly need the item and can afford it, which reduces impulse purchases.

ww.The store will cancel the item that you: The store will not usually cancel an item because you waited a day. Waiting does not cause the item to disappear.
ww.The price always drops overnight, so wai: Prices do not always fall overnight. A waiting period is meant for reflection, not a price drop.
ww.It removes the need for money in any sto: Waiting does not remove the need for money. You still need funds to buy the item.

rw: Correct. If spending exceeds income, the shortfall must come from savings or borrowing, which can lead to debt.

ww.Your debts disappear all at once: Debts do not disappear. Spending more than you earn adds to what you owe.
ww.Your savings automatically grow: Savings fall when you spend more than you earn, so they do not grow automatically.
ww.Your taxes drop to zero this year: Taxes do not drop to zero because of overspending. Taxes depend on income and not on spending.

rw: Correct. Year 1: $1,000 x 1.05 = $1,050. Year 2: $1,050 x 1.05 = $1,102.50, because interest is earned on previous interest.

ww.$1,100.00: $1,100 is simple interest, which uses 5% of the original $1,000 each year. Compound interest also earns interest on interest.
ww.$1,200.00: $1,200 is far too high. A 5% rate over 2 years gives about 10% growth, not 20%.
ww.$1,050.00: $1,050 is the balance after only one year, so it leaves out the second year of growth.

rw: Correct. An emergency fund covers unexpected costs, such as job loss or repairs, so you do not need to borrow or use credit cards.

ww.To pay for vacations and what the family: Vacations and wants are not emergencies. An emergency fund is for unexpected, necessary costs.
ww.To invest in stocks only, for high gains: An emergency fund is kept in safe, liquid accounts, not invested in stocks for high gains.
ww.To avoid saving anywhere else in your li: An emergency fund does not replace other saving. Goals like retirement and large purchases still need savings.

rw: Correct. Divide the goal by the months: $1,200 / 6 = $200 per month.

ww.$120: $120 times 6 months is only $720. To reach $1,200 she must save more each month.
ww.$72: $72 is $1,200 divided by about 17 months. It comes from a miscalculation and falls short of the goal.
ww.$600: $600 is half the goal and would be saved in just two months, not spread over six.

rw: Correct. FDIC insurance protects deposits up to $250,000 per depositor per bank, so a savings account is very safe for short-term money.

ww.Cash kept under a mattress at home: Cash under a mattress can be stolen, lost or destroyed, and it earns no interest, so it is not safe.
ww.A cryptocurrency coin held online: Cryptocurrency prices swing wildly and are not insured, so it is risky for short-term savings.
ww.A single stock in one company: A single stock can lose value quickly and is not suited for short-term money.

rw: Correct. 4.5% APY on $1,000 earns about $45 in a year, the most of these choices because a higher rate gives more interest.

ww.0.5% APY: 0.5% APY on $1,000 earns about $5 in a year, much less than the highest rate offered.
ww.1.0% APY: 1.0% APY earns about $10 in a year, which is less than 4.5%.
ww.0.1% APY: 0.1% APY earns about $1 on $1,000 in a year, the least of these options.

rw: Correct. A certificate of deposit holds your money for a set term at a fixed rate, and early withdrawal usually brings a penalty.

ww.A type of loan that a bank offers to a c: A loan is money you borrow. A CD is money you deposit, so it is a savings product.
ww.A stock share in a large listed company: A stock share is ownership in a company. A CD is a bank deposit that pays interest.
ww.A checking account with no limits on wit: A CD limits withdrawals until maturity, unlike a checking account with easy access.

rw: Correct. Paying yourself first means moving money to savings as soon as you are paid, before spending, which makes saving a habit.

ww.It increases spending every single month: It does not increase spending. Paying yourself first reduces the money available to spend unnecessarily.
ww.It lets you skip saving for a long while: It does the opposite of skipping saving. Savings are set aside first.
ww.It removes the need for any budget: Paying yourself first does not remove the need for a budget. A budget still plans your spending of the remaining money.

rw: Correct. Saving a set percentage of each payment builds savings in good months that can cover lean months.

ww.Spend every payment immediately on whate: Spending every payment immediately leaves nothing for slow months, which makes irregular income harder to manage.
ww.Save nothing until income is steady, the: Waiting for steady income may mean never saving. Irregular earners should save whenever they get paid.
ww.Rely on credit cards instead of saving u: Relying on credit cards creates debt and interest rather than savings.

rw: Correct. Starting early gives interest more time to compound, earning interest on prior interest, so small deposits grow into a larger sum.

ww.Early savers pay no taxes on gains: Savings gains can be taxed, so early savers still may owe taxes on interest.
ww.Interest rates always rise over time: Interest rates do not always rise. They change with the economy, so this is not a reason to start early.
ww.Saving late is simply impossible: Saving late is possible, though harder. Starting early is better because of compounding, not because late saving is impossible.

rw: Correct. $100 per month for 24 months is $100 x 24 = $2,400, with no interest added.

ww.$200: $200 is only 2 months of deposits. She saves for 24 months.
ww.$1,200: $1,200 is only 12 months of deposits, one year rather than two.
ww.$2,000: $2,000 counts 20 months. Two years is 24 months, so $2,400.

rw: Correct. Inflation raises prices, so each dollar buys less over time, which reduces the purchasing power of savings if interest is lower.

ww.It increases purchasing power, as prices: Rising prices reduce purchasing power, not increase it, because each dollar buys fewer goods.
ww.It deletes savings accounts at banks acr: Inflation does not delete accounts. Your balance remains, but its buying power shrinks.
ww.It has no effect on savings or on prices: Inflation does affect savings by eroding buying power, and it is the same as rising prices.

rw: Correct. The real change is about 2% - 3% = -1%, so buying power falls by about 1%.

ww.It rises by about 5%: Buying power does not rise by 5%. Adding the rates is wrong; you subtract inflation from the interest rate.
ww.It stays about equal: It does not stay equal, because 2% interest is below 3% inflation, so prices rise faster than the balance.
ww.It rises by about 1%: It does not rise by 1%. Inflation of 3% beats the 2% interest, so the real change is negative.

rw: Correct. Putting a refund in savings or paying down high-interest debt improves your finances and saves you money on interest.

ww.Ignore it and let the money sit in a dra: Letting money sit unused in a drawer earns nothing and loses buying power to inflation.
ww.Hide it at home in a drawer for years to: Hiding cash at home for years earns no interest and risks theft or loss.
ww.Spend all of it on impulse buys at the m: Spending it all on impulse buys gives short-term enjoyment but no lasting financial benefit.
